45740-the-boy-scouts-of-lakeville-high.title: The Boy Scouts Of Lakeville High
45740-the-boy-scouts-of-lakeville-high.creator: Leslie W. Quirk
45740-the-boy-scouts-of-lakeville-high.description: A book by Leslie W. Quirk. From her perch on the turning-pole, which jutted out of the big butternut tree in the Sefton back lawn, Molly Sefton watched the brick-red thatch and the serious face beneath it. She wondered whether the boy were fifteen years old or sixteen, and whether these new neighbors who had moved in only the day before would prove as "nice" as she had found the rest of the little village of Lakeville.

arxiv-2107-10281.title: Preparing to discover the unknown with Rubin LSST - I: Time domain
arxiv-2107-10281.creator: Xiaolong Li, Fabio Ragosta, William I. Clarkson, Federica B. Bianco
arxiv-2107-10281.description: Abstract Perhaps the most exciting promise of the Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space & Time (LSST) is its capability to discover phenomena never before seen or predicted from theory: true astrophysical novelties, but the ability of LSST to make these discoveries will depend on the survey strategy.

arxiv-2109-02468.title: Secondary frequency control stabilizing voltage dynamics
arxiv-2109-02468.creator: Eder Batista Tchawou Tchuisseu, Eric-Donald Dongmo, Pavel Procházka, Paul Woafo, Pere Colet, Benjamin Schäfer
arxiv-2109-02468.description: Abstract The ongoing energy transition challenges the stability of the electrical power system. Stable operation of the electrical power grid requires both the voltage (amplitude) and the frequency to stay within operational bounds. While much research has focused on frequency dynamics and stability, the voltage dynamics has been neglected.

arxiv-2212-09527.description: Abstract Consider the batch-arrival G ​ I X / M / c / N GI^{X}/M/c/N model with c c servers, general inter-arrival batch times, finite buffer, and exponential service times. Inter-arrival batch times, batch sizes, and service times are i . i . d . i.i.d. and independent of each other.

arxiv-2508-00478.title: CyGATE: Game-Theoretic Cyber Attack-Defense Engine for Patch Strategy Optimization
arxiv-2508-00478.creator: Yuning Jiang 1 , Nay Oo 2 , Qiaoran Meng 1 , Lu Lin 1 , Dusit Niyato 3 , Zehui Xiong 4 , Hoon Wei Lim 2 , Biplab Sikdar 1
arxiv-2508-00478.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuning Jiang 1 , Nay Oo 2 , Qiaoran Meng 1 , Lu Lin 1 , Dusit Niyato 3 , Zehui Xiong 4 , Hoon Wei Lim 2 , Biplab Sikdar 1. Modern cyber attacks unfold through multiple stages, requiring defenders to dynamically prioritize mitigations under uncertainty. While game-theoretic models capture attacker-defender interactions, existing approaches often rely on static assumptions and lack integration with real-time threat intelligence, limiting their adaptability.

arxiv-2508-09864.title: Strong lensing and Hawking spectra of charged black hole under Lorentz violation theory
arxiv-2508-09864.creator: Yenshembam Priyobarta Singh e1,addr1, Ningthoujam Media e2,addr1 Telem Ibungochouba Singh e3,addr1
arxiv-2508-09864.description: Abstract In this paper, we investigate the strong gravitational lensing effects around the Reissner-Nordström-like black hole (RN-like BH) in bumblebee gravity. We calculate the lensing quantities such as deflection angle, radius of the photon sphere, angular separation, relativistic image characteristics, Einstein ring and time delay.

arxiv-2512-21935.creator: Hongjin Wu, Ulrik Brandes
arxiv-2512-21935.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hongjin Wu, Ulrik Brandes. We consider the homogeneous Kuramoto model on a graph and study the geometry of its associated nonconvex energy landscape. This problem admits a dual interpretation. On the one hand, it can be viewed as a geometric optimization problem, seeking configurations of phases that minimize the energy function E ( 𝜽 ) := − ∑ 1 ≤ i , j ≠ n A i ​ j cos ( θ i − θ j ) E(\boldsymbol{\theta}):=-\sum_{1\leq i,j\neq n}A_{ij}\cos(\theta_{i}-\theta_{j}) .

arxiv-2601-04902.title: One-clock synthesis problems
arxiv-2601-04902.creator: Sławomir Lasota, Mathieu Lehaut, Julie Parreaux, Radosław Piórkowski
arxiv-2601-04902.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Sławomir Lasota, Mathieu Lehaut, Julie Parreaux, Radosław Piórkowski. We study a generalisation of Büchi-Landweber games to the timed setting. The winning condition is specified by a non-deterministic timed automaton, and one of the players can elapse time. We perform a systematic study of synthesis problems in all variants of timed games, depending on which player’s winning condition is specified, and which player’s strategy (or controller, a finite-memory strategy) is sought.

arxiv-2602-17787.title: Market Games for Generative Models: Equilibria, Welfare, and Strategic Entry
arxiv-2602-17787.creator: Xiukun Wei, Min Shi, Xueru Zhang
arxiv-2602-17787.description: Abstract Generative model ecosystems increasingly operate as competitive multi-platform markets, where platforms strategically select models from a shared pool and users with heterogeneous preferences choose among them. Understanding how platforms interact, when market equilibria exist, how outcomes are shaped by model-providers, platforms, and user behavior, and how social welfare is affected is critical for fostering a beneficial market environment.

pmc-10648165.creator: Il-Ho Ahn, Dong Jin Lee, Deuk Young Kim, Khaled Saoud, Sami Rtimi, Fadwa El-Mellouhi
pmc-10648165.description: We propose and demonstrate that temperature-dependent curve-fitting error values of the Schottky diode I–V curve in the forward regime can be an auxiliary diagnostic signal as the temperature-scan Capacitance DLTS (CDLTS) signals and helps to work time-efficiently with high accuracy when using the Laplace Transform (LT)–DLTS or Isothermal Capacitance transient spectroscopy (ICTS) method.

pmc-11450286.title: Nutritional Composition and Effect of Loquat Fruit (Eriobotrya japonica L. var. Navela) on Lipid Metabolism and Liver Steatosis in High-Fat High-Sucrose Diet-Fed Mice
pmc-11450286.creator: Imane Mokhtari, Mohammadine Moumou, Chakib Mokhtari, Mohamed Harnafi, Dragan Milenkovic, Souliman Amrani, Hicham Harnafi
pmc-11450286.description: Loquat (Eriobotrya japonica L.) is a popular fruit known for its sweet and slightly tangy flavor, which is widely consumed both fresh and in various processed forms. This study aimed to analyze the biochemical composition of loquat juice and investigate its metabolic benefits in mice fed a high-fat/high-sucrose diet (HFSD).

pmc-11535370.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices of patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) towards Anti-VEGF treatment under one-stop intravitreal injection model
pmc-11535370.creator: Liangzhang Tan, Zhiqiong Ma, Qi Miao, Shoukuan Liu, Yongtao Li, Yifeng Ke, Xinjun Ren
pmc-11535370.description: To evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) regarding anti-VEGF treatment within a one-stop intravitreal injection service model. A cross-sectional study was conducted from July 1, 2023, to January 31, 2024, at the One-stop Intravitreal Injection Center at Tianjin Medical University Eye Hospital. Data were collected using a specially designed KAP questionnaire.

pmc-11713145.title: Do the effects of Hormone Replacement Therapy during menopause differ by APOE genotype?
pmc-11713145.creator: Emily Budden, Sam Atkinson, Sam Berens, Alice Stanton, Sarah L King, Anne‐Marie Minihane, Michael Hornberger, Daniel Reisel, Louise Newson, Naji Tabet, Dorina Cadar, Claire L Lancaster
pmc-11713145.description: BackgroundReported effects of Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) on late‐life neurodegenerative disease are inconsistent. Variability in the timing and formulation of HRT, plus whether an individual carries an Apolipoprotein (APOE) e4 genetic risk variant for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD), likely contribute to conflicting results.

pmc-12623142.title: Scalp Actinomycosis Presenting as Chronic Discharging Sinuses: A Rare Case Report
pmc-12623142.creator: Muhammad Umar Ahsan, Muhammad Saeed, Hafiz Arslan Mahmood, Nisar Ahmed, Somaiya Ahmed, Arooj Khan, Saba Shaheen
pmc-12623142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Actinomycosis is a rare, chronic granulomatous infection caused by anaerobic, filamentous bacteria of the genus Actinomyces, typically involving the cervicofacial, thoracic, or abdominopelvic regions. Scalp involvement is exceptionally rare and frequently misdiagnosed as a neoplastic or tubercular condition. We report the case of a 47‐year‐old male tandoor worker with a three‐year history of recurrent scalp infections who presented with firm, non‐tender swellings over the parietal and occipital scalp, complicated by discharging sinus tracts.

pmc-12678177.title: Increased arterial stiffness and atherosclerosis in patients with nonfunctioning adrenal incidentaloma
pmc-12678177.creator: Mirko Parasiliti-Caprino, Elisa Febbraro, Bartolomeo Sangermano, Daniele Giuseppe Candela, Stefano Arata, Matteo Procopio, Martina Bollati, Chiara Lopez, Ezio Ghigo, Mauro Maccario
pmc-12678177.description: Nonfunctioning adrenal incidentalomas (NFAIs) are typically considered benign and hormonally inactive, yet emerging evidence suggests a potential association with increased cardiovascular risk. This study aimed to evaluate whether NFAIs are independently associated with vascular damage, assessed through arterial stiffness and carotid Doppler ultrasound.

pmc-13018763.title: Why administration of lethal drugs should not be the role of the doctor
pmc-13018763.creator: Sally Barker, Zoë Fritz, Alexander Ruck Keene
pmc-13018763.description: The suitability of doctors as agents of assisting dying remains debated, although it is common in many jurisdictions, and forms part of the proposed assisted dying legislation for England and Wales.We examine the established philosophical and legal role of doctors in England and Wales and compare it to the active role required of doctors under proposed assisted dying legislation.

pmc-13028799.title: Enhanced Biocontrol of Cotton Verticillium Wilt Through Optimized Solid-State Fermentation of Myxococcus fulvus KS01 Using Insect Frass as a Matrix
pmc-13028799.creator: Jian Han, Yongcheng Chen, Qiang Sheng, Wei Lu, Ming Luo, Benzhong Fu, Deying Ma
pmc-13028799.description: Cotton Verticillium wilt, caused by Verticillium dahliae, is a devastating soil-borne disease that severely limits global cotton production. While Myxococcus fulvus KS01 has demonstrated potent antagonistic activity and multi-functional biocontrol effects against V. dahliae, its practical application has been hindered by low myxospore yields and inconsistent efficacy in initial solid-state fermentation (SSF).

pmc-13088520.title: Multifunctional MoS₂-PMMA bone cement with enhanced strength and antibacterial activity to overcome limitations of conventional materials in orthopedic surgery
pmc-13088520.creator: Changsheng Gong, ShengBo Shi, ZiJing Zhang, ZeTian Zhao, Zuo Liu, Zhe Wang, Xiaobing Yu
pmc-13088520.description: BackgroundsThe increasing incidence of osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) necessitates the development of effective treatment strategies. Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement, which is widely used, lacks adequate antimicrobial properties and poses the risk of postoperative infections. Molybdenum disulfide (MoS₂) nanosheets, which are known for their antimicrobial and osteogenic potential, offer a novel approach.

pmc-13356773.title: Sociodemographic Determinants of Timely Hip Dysplasia Ultrasound Screening
pmc-13356773.creator: CeAnn Romanaggi, Julianna Mazziotti, Spencer Smith, Jung Yoo, Matthew Halsey
pmc-13356773.description: BackgroundBreech presentation is a strong risk factor for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), a condition that, when diagnosed late, can lead to poor outcomes. Accordingly, it is recommended that breech-born infants undergo hip ultrasound (US) screening at 6 weeks or receive an anteriorpostierior (AP) pelvic radiograph at 6 months of age to enable early detection and timely intervention.

pmc-13418389.title: Nutrition knowledge and bone health: development and validation of the ‘NutriBone’ questionnaire for Italian adult women
pmc-13418389.creator: Silvia Callegaro, Kyriaki Apergi, Francesca Scazzina, Daniela Martini, Donato Angelino, Alice Bongrani, Alice Rosi, Giovanni Passeri
pmc-13418389.description: Objective:This study aimed to develop and validate a questionnaire assessing the nutrition knowledge (NK) of Italian adult women regarding the relationship between diet, lifestyle and bone health.Design:A thirty-item questionnaire in Italian was developed by experts based on a literature review. Participants completed the questionnaire twice, with a 2–4 week gap between the two administrations.

pmc-13622337.title: Edge effects on parasitoid hymenopteran biodiversity in canola fields
pmc-13622337.creator: Abbe Pawluk, Jenny L McCune, Robert A Laird, Héctor A Cárcamo, Nathan Haan
pmc-13622337.description: Parasitoid hymenopterans are highly valuable pest control agents. Despite their necessity within the agriculture industry, they remain one of the most understudied groups of insects. Non-crop habitats adjacent to farmland provide critical ecological services for these beneficial insects and can act as a corridor from uncultivated land to fields; this interaction is a form of edge effect.

pmc-13680377.title: Human targeting of morphologically unique fishes amplifies the risk of functional erosion
pmc-13680377.creator: Pierre Bouchet, Sébastien Brosse, Aurèle Toussaint
pmc-13680377.description: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity.

pmc-13722868.title: Auxin-mediated RcARF8-RcWRKY29-RcERF98 module protects the rose petals against the Botrytis cinerea by modulating ascorbic acid biosynthesis and reactive oxygen species scavenging
pmc-13722868.creator: Jie Wu, Mengyue Jing, Shiqiu Yang, Qiushi Li, Daliang Li, Qi Fu, Xujun Ma, Dan Wang, Jiaxing Li, Hongying Jian, Huijun Yan, Kaixue Tang, Hao Zhang, Xianqin Qiu, Weikun Jing
pmc-13722868.description: As one of the world’s most important ornamental crops, rose (Rosa sp.) is highly susceptible to grey mold disease caused by Botrytis cinerea. Outbreaks of this disease during long-distance transportation often lead to substantial economic losses. This study identifies the WRKY transcription factor RcWRKY29 as a key regulator in the defense response against B. cinerea.
